metadata.title: Dropout: A Simple Way to Prevent Neural Networks from Overfitting
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Dropout
nodes.statement: A regularization technique that randomly drops units (along with their connections) from a neural network during training, where each unit is retained with fixed probability $p$ independent of other units.
nodes.statement_clean: Randomly remove neural network units during training, retaining each with probability p.

nodes.name: Thinned Network
nodes.statement: Given a neural network with $n$ units, applying dropout produces a thinned network consisting of all units that survived dropout; the original net can be seen as a collection of $2^n$ possible thinned networks sharing weights.
nodes.statement_clean: A subnetwork sampled by retaining a random subset of units; the parent net of n units defines 2^n thinned nets sharing weights.

nodes.name: Standard Feed-Forward Operation
nodes.statement: For a network with $L$ hidden layers, $l \in \{1,\ldots,L\}$, the feed-forward operation is $z_i^{(l+1)} = w_i^{(l+1)} y^{(l)} + b_i^{(l+1)}$ and $y_i^{(l+1)} = f(z_i^{(l+1)})$, where $f$ is any activation function (e.g. $f(x)=1/(1+\exp(-x))$).
nodes.statement_clean: Standard layer-wise feed-forward computation with weights, biases, and an activation function.

nodes.name: Dropout Feed-Forward Operation
nodes.statement: With dropout: $r_j^{(l)} \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)$, $\tilde{y}^{(l)} = r^{(l)} \ast y^{(l)}$, $z_i^{(l+1)} = w_i^{(l+1)} \tilde{y}^{(l)} + b_i^{(l+1)}$, $y_i^{(l+1)} = f(z_i^{(l+1)})$, where $\ast$ is the element-wise product.
nodes.statement_clean: Layer-wise feed-forward with each unit's output multiplied element-wise by an independent Bernoulli(p) mask.

nodes.name: Weight Scaling at Test Time
nodes.statement: At test time, the trained weights are scaled as $W^{(l)}_{\text{test}} = p\,W^{(l)}$ and the network is used without dropout; this matches the expected output at training time.
nodes.statement_clean: At test time, multiply each weight by p and run a single deterministic network.

nodes.name: Max-norm Regularization
nodes.statement: Constrain the norm of the incoming weight vector at each hidden unit by $\|w\|_2 \le c$, enforced by projecting $w$ onto the surface of a ball of radius $c$ whenever it leaves.
nodes.statement_clean: Cap the L2 norm of each unit's incoming weights at a constant c via projection.

nodes.name: Restricted Boltzmann Machine (RBM)
nodes.statement: An undirected graphical model with visible units $v \in \{0,1\}^D$ and hidden units $h \in \{0,1\}^F$ defining $P(h,v;\theta) = \frac{1}{Z(\theta)} \exp(v^\top W h + a^\top h + b^\top v)$, with parameters $\theta = \{W,a,b\}$ and partition function $Z$.
nodes.statement_clean: An energy-based undirected model on binary visible/hidden units with bipartite connections.

nodes.name: Dropout RBM
nodes.statement: An RBM augmented with binary mask $r \in \{0,1\}^F$, $r_j \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)$, with joint $P(r,h,v;p,\theta) = P(r;p) P(h,v|r;\theta)$ where $g(h_j,r_j) = \mathbf{1}(r_j=1) + \mathbf{1}(r_j=0)\mathbf{1}(h_j=0)$ enforces $h_j=0$ whenever $r_j=0$.
nodes.statement_clean: An RBM whose hidden units are masked by independent Bernoulli(p) variables; masked-out units must be zero.

nodes.name: Multiplicative Gaussian Noise (Gaussian Dropout)
nodes.statement: Replace Bernoulli(p) masks with multiplicative noise $r' \sim \mathcal{N}(1,\sigma^2)$, perturbing each hidden activation as $h_i \mapsto h_i r'$; expected activation is unchanged so no test-time weight scaling is required.
nodes.statement_clean: Multiply hidden activations by Gaussian noise with mean 1 instead of Bernoulli masks.

nodes.name: Code Quality (Alternative Splicing Metric)
nodes.statement: $\sum_{i=1}^{|\text{data}|} \sum_{t \in \text{tissues}} \sum_{s \in \{\mathrm{inc,exc,nc}\}} p_{i,t}^s \log(q_t^s(r_i)/\bar{p}^s)$, the negative KL divergence between target $p$ and predicted $q$ distributions; higher is better.
nodes.statement_clean: Negative KL divergence summed over data points, tissues, and splice states.

nodes.name: Overfitting in Deep Neural Networks
nodes.statement: Deep neural nets with many parameters easily overfit, especially with limited training data; the goal is to reduce generalization error without combining many separately trained large nets at test time.
nodes.statement_clean: Reduce neural-network overfitting and approximate model averaging without prohibitive test-time cost.

nodes.name: Linear Regression with Marginalized Dropout
nodes.statement: Given $X \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times D}$, $y \in \mathbb{R}^N$, find $w$ minimizing $\mathbb{E}_{R \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)}\left[\|y - (R \ast X) w\|^2\right]$, where $R$ is a $\{0,1\}^{N \times D}$ Bernoulli mask.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimize the expected squared error of linear regression when inputs are dropped out.

nodes.name: Dropout Training (Stochastic Gradient Descent on Thinned Networks)
nodes.statement: Train dropout neural networks by SGD: for each minibatch case, sample a thinned network and run forward/backprop only on it; gradients are averaged across minibatch cases. Often combined with momentum, decaying learning rates, and max-norm regularization.
nodes.statement_clean: Per-case sampled-thinned-net SGD with optional max-norm, momentum, and decaying learning rate.
input: Retention probabilities $p$ (typically 0.5 for hidden, 0.8 for input)
output: Test-time network with weights $p W^{(l)}$ used without dropout

nodes.name: Monte-Carlo Model Averaging at Test Time
nodes.section: 7.5 Monte-Carlo Model Averaging vs. Weight Scaling
nodes.statement: For each test case, sample $k$ thinned networks using dropout and average their predictions; as $k \to \infty$ this approaches the true model average. Empirically $k \approx 50$ matches the weight-scaling approximation on MNIST.
nodes.statement_clean: Approximate the model average by averaging predictions of k dropout-sampled networks.

nodes.name: Dropout Finetuning of Pretrained Networks
nodes.statement: Pretrain network with stacks of RBMs / autoencoders / DBMs; scale resulting weights up by $1/p$ so that the expected dropout output matches the pretrained output; then finetune with dropout using a smaller learning rate to preserve pretrained information.
nodes.statement_clean: Scale pretrained weights by 1/p, then finetune with dropout using a small learning rate.

nodes.name: Dropout RBM Learning (CD-1 with Mask)
nodes.statement: Apply Contrastive Divergence (CD-1) to dropout RBMs: per training case, first sample $r$, then use only retained hidden units for the CD update; a different $r$ is sampled for each minibatch case.
nodes.statement_clean: CD-1 over a sampled hidden-unit mask r, refreshed per training case.

nodes.name: RBM Joint Distribution
nodes.statement: $P(h,v;\theta) = \frac{1}{Z(\theta)} \exp(v^\top W h + a^\top h + b^\top v)$.

nodes.name: Dropout RBM Conditional
nodes.statement: $P(h_j = 1 | r_j, v) = \mathbf{1}(r_j = 1)\,\sigma\!\left(b_j + \sum_i W_{ij} v_i\right)$.

nodes.name: Marginalized Dropout Linear Regression Objective
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}_{R \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)}\!\left[\|y - (R \ast X) w\|^2\right] = \|y - p X w\|^2 + p(1-p)\|\Gamma w\|^2$, where $\Gamma = (\mathrm{diag}(X^\top X))^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Reparameterized Dropout Regression
nodes.statement: With $\tilde{w} = p w$: $\|y - X \tilde{w}\|^2 + \frac{1-p}{p} \|\Gamma \tilde{w}\|^2$.

nodes.name: Dropout Regression Equivalent to Ridge with Data-Dependent Penalty
nodes.statement: In expectation, dropout linear regression is equivalent to ridge regression with penalty matrix $\Gamma = (\mathrm{diag}(X^\top X))^{1/2}$, scaling the weight cost of $w_i$ by the standard deviation of dimension $i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Marginalized dropout for linear regression equals ridge regression with feature-std-scaled penalty.
conclusions: $\mathbb{E}_R\!\left[\|y - (R \ast X) w\|^2\right] = \|y - p X w\|^2 + p(1-p)\|\Gamma w\|^2$
Equivalent to ridge regression with weight-cost scaled by feature standard deviations

nodes.name: Dropout Approximates Geometric Mean of Exponentially Many Models
nodes.statement: At test time, applying weights $p\,W^{(l)}$ to a single un-thinned network approximately combines the predictions of the $2^n$ thinned networks via an equally weighted geometric mean, ensuring expected hidden outputs match.
nodes.statement_clean: Test-time weight scaling approximates an equally weighted geometric mean of all 2^n thinned subnetworks.
assumptions: Network of $n$ units trained with dropout retention probability $p$
conclusions: Single test net with weights $p W$ approximates the average of $2^n$ thinned nets
Expected hidden output under dropout equals deterministic test output

nodes.name: Same Mean and Variance for Bernoulli and Gaussian Dropout
nodes.statement: Bernoulli dropout multiplied so $r_b \in \{0, 1/p\}$ has $E[r_b]=1$, $\mathrm{Var}[r_b] = (1-p)/p$; setting $\sigma^2 = (1-p)/p$ in $r_g \sim \mathcal{N}(1,\sigma^2)$ gives $E[r_g]=1$, $\mathrm{Var}[r_g]=(1-p)/p$. $r_g$ has highest entropy and $r_b$ the lowest among such matched-moment noises.
nodes.statement_clean: Bernoulli and Gaussian dropout can be matched to identical mean and variance; Gaussian has higher entropy.
conclusions: $r_g$ has highest entropy, $r_b$ lowest, among noises with these first two moments

nodes.name: Sparsity as Side-Effect of Dropout
nodes.statement: Dropout induces sparse hidden-unit activations even without an explicit sparsity regularizer: the mean activation drops from about 2.0 to about 0.7 on the MNIST autoencoder, with a sharp peak at zero.

nodes.name: Network-Size Heuristic for Dropout
nodes.statement: If an $n$-sized layer is optimal for a standard net, a dropout net should have at least $n/p$ units, so the expected number of retained units matches the optimal standard size.

nodes.name: Learning Rate and Momentum Heuristics
nodes.statement: Dropout nets typically need learning rates 10-100 times those optimal for standard nets, plus momentum values around 0.95-0.99 (vs. 0.9), to compensate for the noisy gradients introduced by dropout.

nodes.name: Drawback: Increased Training Time
nodes.statement: A dropout network typically takes 2-3 times longer to train than a standard network of the same architecture because each case effectively trains a different random architecture, producing very noisy gradients.

nodes.name: MNIST Classification with Dropout
nodes.statement: On the 28x28 MNIST digit classification task, dropout reduces error from 1.60% (standard NN, Simard et al. 2003) to 1.35%; with ReLU + max-norm + larger architecture down to 0.95%; DBM-pretrained dropout net reaches 0.79% (best known permutation-invariant result). $p=0.5$ for hidden units, $p=0.8$ for inputs.

nodes.name: SVHN Classification with Dropout ConvNet
nodes.statement: On 32x32 SVHN house-number digit classification, a ConvNet with three conv+max-pool layers and 2 FC layers achieves 3.95% error; dropout in FC layers only reduces to 3.02%; dropout in all layers reduces to 2.55%. Layer retention probabilities $p = (0.9, 0.75, 0.75, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5)$.

nodes.name: CIFAR-10 / CIFAR-100 with Dropout ConvNet
nodes.statement: Without data augmentation, dropout in FC layers reduces CIFAR-10 error from 14.98% to 14.32%; dropout in all layers reduces it to 12.61%; on CIFAR-100, dropout reduces error from 43.48% to 37.20%.

nodes.name: ImageNet ILSVRC-2010/2012 with Dropout ConvNet
nodes.statement: On ILSVRC-2010, ConvNet+dropout achieves top-1/top-5 error 37.5%/17.0% (vs. ~45-47% / 25-28% for prior SIFT-based methods); on ILSVRC-2012, an ensemble of 5 ConvNets+dropout wins the competition with 16.4% top-5 test error.

nodes.name: TIMIT Speech Recognition with Dropout
nodes.statement: On the TIMIT phone recognition task using 21-frame log-filter-bank windows, a 6-layer net achieves 23.4% PER; dropout reduces it to 21.8%; DBN-pretrained 4-layer net + dropout reaches 19.7% (vs. 22.7% without dropout).

nodes.name: Reuters-RCV1 Document Classification
nodes.section: 6.3 Results on a Text Data Set
nodes.statement: On a 50-class subset of Reuters-RCV1 (vocabulary 2000), the best non-dropout neural net achieves 31.05% error; adding dropout reduces error to 29.62%, a smaller gain than for vision/speech.

nodes.name: Alternative Splicing (RNA Features)
nodes.statement: On the Xiong et al. 2011 alternative-splicing data set, dropout NN achieves Code Quality 567 bits, beating standard NN with early stopping (440), regression+PCA (463), and SVM+PCA (487); only Bayesian NN (623) is higher.

nodes.name: MNIST Comparison of Regularizers
nodes.statement: On MNIST with a 784-1024-1024-2048-10 ReLU network, L2 gives 1.62%, L2+L1 1.60%, L2+KL-sparsity 1.55%, max-norm 1.35%, dropout+L2 1.25%, dropout+max-norm 1.05% (lowest).

nodes.name: Effect of Dropout Rate p (Architecture Fixed and pn Fixed)
nodes.statement: On MNIST 784-2048-2048-2048-10: with $n$ fixed, error is flat for $0.4 \le p \le 0.8$ and rises near $p=1$; with $pn$ fixed (so smaller $p$ gives larger nets), error stays low even at $p=0.1$ and the optimum is near $p \approx 0.6$.

nodes.name: Effect of Data Set Size
nodes.statement: Dropout gives no improvement for very small training sets (100, 500 MNIST examples); the gain grows with set size up to a sweet spot, then declines once overfitting is no longer an issue.

nodes.name: Monte-Carlo Averaging vs. Weight Scaling
nodes.section: 7.5 Monte-Carlo Model Averaging vs. Weight Scaling
nodes.statement: On MNIST, the Monte-Carlo $k$-sample average matches the weight-scaling approximation around $k \approx 50$ and stays within one standard deviation thereafter, supporting weight scaling as a good approximation of the true model average.

nodes.name: Bernoulli vs. Gaussian Dropout
nodes.statement: On MNIST (2 layers x 1024), Bernoulli dropout gives 1.08+/-0.04% vs. Gaussian dropout 0.95+/-0.04%; on CIFAR-10 (3 conv + 2 FC), 12.6+/-0.1% vs. 12.5+/-0.1%, with $\sigma = \sqrt{(1-p)/p}$.

nodes.name: Features Learned With and Without Dropout
nodes.statement: Single-hidden-layer 256-ReLU MNIST autoencoder: without dropout the units co-adapt and individually do not detect meaningful features; with $p=0.5$ dropout the units detect edges, strokes, and spots in different image parts.

nodes.name: Dropout RBM Features and Sparsity
nodes.statement: On MNIST with 256 hidden units, the dropout RBM ($p=0.5$) learns coarser features than a standard RBM with fewer dead units, and produces much sparser hidden activations even without an explicit sparsity regularizer.

nodes.name: Derivation of Marginalized Dropout for Linear Regression
nodes.statement: By expanding $\mathbb{E}_R\|y - (R \ast X) w\|^2$ and using independence of the Bernoulli mask entries, one obtains $\|y - p X w\|^2 + p(1-p)\|\Gamma w\|^2$ with $\Gamma = (\mathrm{diag}(X^\top X))^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Expand expected squared error
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}_R\|y - (R \ast X) w\|^2 = \|y\|^2 - 2 y^\top \mathbb{E}_R[(R \ast X)] w + \mathbb{E}_R[w^\top (R \ast X)^\top (R \ast X) w]$.

nodes.name: Use Bernoulli mean and variance
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}[R_{ij}] = p$ and $\mathrm{Var}[R_{ij}] = p(1-p)$, so $\mathbb{E}_R[(R \ast X)] = p X$ and the off-diagonal cross-terms in $X^\top X$ get coefficient $p^2$ while diagonal entries get $p$.

nodes.name: Collect deterministic plus penalty form
nodes.statement: Combining gives $\|y - p X w\|^2 + p(1-p) \sum_i (X^\top X)_{ii} w_i^2 = \|y - p X w\|^2 + p(1-p)\|\Gamma w\|^2$ with $\Gamma = (\mathrm{diag}(X^\top X))^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Sample dropout masks
nodes.statement: For each training case in the minibatch and each layer $l$, sample $r_j^{(l)} \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)$ independently across units.

nodes.name: Forward pass on thinned net
nodes.statement: Compute $\tilde{y}^{(l)} = r^{(l)} \ast y^{(l)}$ and propagate $z_i^{(l+1)} = w_i^{(l+1)} \tilde{y}^{(l)} + b_i^{(l+1)}$, $y_i^{(l+1)} = f(z_i^{(l+1)})$ through all layers.

nodes.name: Backpropagate gradients on thinned net
nodes.statement: Backpropagate the loss only through units that survived dropout; parameters not used by a case receive zero gradient from it. Average gradients across the minibatch.

nodes.name: Apply max-norm projection
nodes.statement: After each update, project each unit's incoming weight vector $w$ onto $\|w\|_2 \le c$ (max-norm constraint) whenever it leaves the ball.

nodes.name: Set test-time scaled network
nodes.statement: After training, set $W^{(l)}_{\text{test}} = p W^{(l)}$ and use the deterministic feed-forward network without dropout for predictions.
